requirements.evidence: Contract and behaviour are mostly there: migrations with `entities_slug_unique`, `owner_seq` storedAs + `entity_memberships_one_owner` (2026_10_29_000002:19-22); policies match the rules (EntityPolicy.php, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:40-55); HomeController 0/1/>1 dispatch; pick sets the session only after the membership check and logs on `audit` (EntityPickController.php:14-24); CreateEntity retries up to 5 times and calls uniqueSlug() on each attempt (CreateEntity.php:29-58); switcher markup (`is-link` + `data-current="1"`, `is-light`); navbar link only when count > 1; lang keys in both locales. Gaps: membership counts include memberships of soft-deleted entities, so with one membership whose entity is trashed `$membership->entity->id` is null-dereferenced (HomeController.php:22-25, ResolveCurrentEntity.php:48-50); the retry also treats every 23000 error (e.g. FK) as a slug collision.

conventions.evidence: The domain write is done inline in the Livewire component (`Entity::create` + `memberships()->create` in CreateEntity.php:33-44) instead of an `app/Actions/CreateEntity` that authorizes. Authorization is hand-rolled `membershipFor(...) === null -> abort(403)` in Dashboard.php:17 and EntityPickController.php:14 when the new EntityPolicy::view exists and should be used. No tests at all despite the TDD rule, no CHANGELOG entry, and migrations with hand-made `000001`/`000002` timestamps. Good points: `#[Validate]` + `$this->validate()`, `$fillable` set, docs/database-schema.md updated, `{{ }}` escaping, existing `x-form-field`/`x-button` components reused.

security.evidence: Owner role is server-set (`'role' => UserRole::Owner`, CreateEntity.php:42) and `name` is validated. Pick checks membership before touching the session. Dashboard mount enforces membership of the requested entity (Dashboard.php:17), so a valid session for another entity does not grant access. Output is escaped. Smaller gaps: CreateEntity::submit has no `$this->authorize('create', Entity::class)` and no rate limit on entity creation. The custom `current_entity` middleware is not registered with `Livewire::addPersistentMiddleware` (the dashboard has no actions yet, so impact is limited).

tests.evidence: The diff contains no test files: nothing for the migrations or owner constraint, the policies, middleware, home dispatch, pick, onboarding (including the slug-collision retry) or dashboard 403. There are also no unauthorized or tamper tests for the Livewire component, which the Livewire policy requires.

simplicity.evidence: The 0/1/>1 membership dispatch is duplicated almost line for line between HomeController.php:14-30 and ResolveCurrentEntity.php:41-57. setContext stores the entity in three places (request attribute, `app()->instance('current_entity')` and a scoped `CurrentEntity` holder; ResolveCurrentEntity.php:61-67), and none of them is read anywhere in the diff. The update and delete bodies in EntityPolicy are copy-pasted. EntityMembershipPolicy::delete re-derives the enum even though `role` is already cast (lines 42-44).

readability.evidence: Classes are small and clearly named. The retry loop is readable but uses the magic `4`/`5` and string-matched error messages (CreateEntity.php:49-56). The PHPDoc on User::entities() wrongly says `BelongsToMany<User, $this>` (User.php:31). Style otherwise matches the sibling files.

scope.evidence: Everything in the diff serves the task. No members or settings pages, no locale middleware, no navbar redesign. The docs edit is the requested database-schema.md update.

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests for any new behaviour. This breaks the project's mandatory TDD rule and the Livewire definition of done (unauthorized and tamper tests).
Creating the entity and its owner membership is a domain write, so it should live in an `app/Actions` class that authorizes, not inline in the Livewire component.
Both places hand-roll membership checks with abort(403) instead of `authorize('view', $entity)` through the new EntityPolicy, which goes against 'authorization always goes through policies'.
The public submit() action never calls $this->authorize('create', Entity::class) and is not rate-limited, both of which the Livewire security policy requires.
Membership counts include memberships of soft-deleted entities. A user whose only entity is trashed hits a null `$membership->entity` and gets an error instead of being sent to onboarding.
Any SQLSTATE 23000 error (for example an FK violation) is treated as a slug collision and retried, instead of only the `entities_slug_unique` violation.
The membership dispatch logic is duplicated, and the tenant context is stored three ways that nothing reads.
The docs-sync convention asks for an `[Unreleased]` CHANGELOG entry, and none was added.
The custom `current_entity` middleware is not registered as Livewire persistent middleware, so it will not apply on later /livewire/update requests once the dashboard gets actions.
The PHPDoc generic says BelongsToMany<User, $this>, but the relation returns Entity.

review.summary: The change builds the full entity data model, policies, tenant middleware, home dispatch, pick, onboarding with slug-collision retry, switcher, dashboard, lang keys and schema docs, and the core logic is largely correct and secure. It ships no tests at all, though, which is mandatory under the project's TDD and Livewire policy. It also skips the Actions layer for the domain write, uses inline abort(403) checks instead of the new policies, and duplicates the dispatch logic, so it needs substantial rework before approval.
